one_liner: A wide-moat business worth owning, but it trades at 2.7x fair value. Interesting below about $80.

profile.what: Ecolab provides water treatment, cleaning and hygiene products and services to restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food and drink producers, data centres and heavy industry.
profile.money: It sells chemicals and dispensing systems together with regular visits from its own technicians. Customers pay for the result, such as clean dishes or protected equipment, more than for the chemical.
profile.valued: Ecolab is valued on P/E at a premium for steady growth and pricing power. The multiple depends on margin expansion and raw-material costs.

summary.sentence: The hygiene and water-treatment leader, back to full margins and fully priced.
strengths: Revenue has grown every year in the record.
Gross margin has recovered to a five-year high.
Current assets comfortably exceed current liabilities.
risks: Valued at a high forward multiple.
Margins fell when raw-material costs jumped in fiscal 2022.
Sales follow restaurant and hotel activity.

meaning.what_it_does: Supplies cleaning, sanitising and water-treatment products and services to restaurants, hotels, hospitals, food plants and industrial sites.
meaning.how_it_makes_money: Chemicals and dispensing equipment sold with on-site service from its own field staff.
meaning.how_it_keeps_making_money: Its technicians are inside customers' operations every week, and the products are a tiny part of their costs.
meaning.how_it_could_stop: Raw-material costs spike faster than it can raise prices, as happened in fiscal 2022.

moat.summary: The largest field-service force in its industry; customers will not risk a hygiene failure to save a little.

industry.summary: Cleaning and water treatment change slowly; water scarcity is raising demand.

management.summary: Decades of dividend increases and a clear focus on raising margins.

financial_health.ratio_gaps: Not available from the data source, so not shown: a ten-year record, inventory and receivables turnover, the quick ratio, goodwill and tangible book value, and maintenance capex split from growth capex. Owner earnings therefore deduct all capex, which is conservative.

valuation.method: Fair value is the average of two methods: (1) Owner cash flow: $1.7B a year: free cash flow less stock-based pay (median of the last three fiscal years and TTM). (2) Damodaran: cash flow to the firm: Sales grow 5–11% for five years, fading to 3%; operating margin held at 18%; cost of capital 8.4%. Cash added, debt subtracted. The owner cash flow method grows the cash for five years, then at half that rate, 3% after year ten, discounted at 10%. Stock-based pay is deducted because it is a real cost to owners.
